newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin may fight back if deputies try to oust him.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin may fight back if deputies try to oust him.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin's representative in parliament warned deputies on Wednesday they could face a tough response if they try to oust the Kremlin leader on health grounds.

Alexander Kotenkov told the State Duma lower house that a resolution it was considering on removing the president would not have any legal force if it was approved, but that it would have dangerous implications.
"There would be no reaction to this if it couldn't harm the state in a most dramatic way," Kotenkov told deputies.
He added: "The phrase 'The President is dismissed' may be taken by some members of society as an excuse not to carry out presidential orders.

"There is a legal term 'the prevention of greater harm'. When discussing this draft I call on you to imagine what measures might be taken by other branches of power to prevent a greater harm," he said.
He did not say what measures the Kremlin had in mind.
The pro-government "Our Home is Russia" group and the liberal opposition "Yabloko" party walked out of the chamber.
"I call on you not to take part in this humiliating show," "Our Home" leader Sergei Belyaev told the chamber before the walkout.
